# Single-Source-of-Truth Generators

Hold the facts **once**, in a plain data structure, and emit every deliverable from it — including
deliverables in different formats and for different audiences. The test of the pattern is not "is
there a generator"; it is **can any two outputs disagree**. If they can, it is not this pattern.

Confirmed twice in `Information-Systems-Modelling`, in two consecutive labs written the same day.

## Lab 7 — one spec, three artefacts

`lab7/src/specs.js` (605 lines) declares each of eight business processes once: pools, lanes, nodes
with event markers, sequence flows, message flows. A zero-dependency Node generator
(`layout.js` 307 · `svg.js` 298 · `bpmn.js` 134 · `report-text.js` 49) turns each spec into a
rendered **SVG**, a Camunda-compatible **`.bpmn` file with diagram interchange**, and a section of
the **PDF report**. The README states the reason in the same breath as the mechanism:

> "A zero-dependency Node generator holds the eight processes **once** as a data model and emits the
> diagrams, the BPMN files and the report from it, so the rendered SVG and the `.bpmn` diagram
> interchange can never drift."
> — Information-Systems-Modelling/lab7/README.md, 2026-07-09

"Can never drift" is the load-bearing claim, and here it is structurally true: the SVG and the
`.bpmn` are two renderings of one object, not two documents about one process. See
[[bpmn-process-modelling]].

## Lab 6 — one dataset, two RDF syntaxes

`lab6/app/data/*.json` holds the instance data; one renderer emits **RDFa 1.1** in the body and
**JSON-LD** in the head of every page, plus the static site and the SSR responses. The README is
explicit that this replaced a hand-written version, and names the failure it was replacing:

> "The old approach hand-wrote the same data into six HTML files **twice** (RDFa in the body +
> JSON-LD in the head), so every fact lived in 2–4 places and could drift. This app makes the data
> the single source of truth and **generates** the markup."
> — Information-Systems-Modelling/lab6/app/README.md, 2026-07-09

The switch is a recorded decision with a deletion behind it — see
[[generate-markup-instead-of-hand-writing-it]] — and it is the only place in the fifteen-repo source
set where a superseded version was **deleted** rather than kept.

`src/rdf/vocabmap.js` extends the idea to the documentation *about* the output: the `VOCAB MAP`
comment at the top of each page is generated by walking that page's own graph, so a term added to
the data cannot leave the comment stale. See [[linked-data-publishing]] and
[[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]].

## Why it keeps appearing next to zero-dependency Node

Both instances are `dependencies: {}` with `node:` builtins only, and so is the exam trainer in the
same repo — see [[zero-dependency-no-build-step]]. That is not a coincidence: a generator you own
end to end has no upstream to track, so the cost of *not* taking a diagramming library or a
templating engine is one afternoon of `layout.js`, and the benefit is that the pipeline still runs
in five years.

## The limit of the pattern in this repo

Lab 6's headline principle is that no fact should be written twice. Meanwhile `ontology.ttl` exists
as **byte-identical copies** in `lab5/.../resources/` and `lab6/vocabulary/` — the one fact the
generators do not own is duplicated across the lab boundary, and the prose does not mention it. The
generators guarantee consistency *within* a lab, not *across* the repo. Compare
[[keep-the-superseded-version-in-tree]], which explains why nothing gets deduplicated here.

The narrower sibling pattern — where the generated file and its *input* both live in the tree, with
a DO-NOT-EDIT banner on the output — is [[generated-artifact-with-pristine-source]].
